title: GPU utilization event slice and throttle diagnostic - May 2026
content:
Purpose
This is a focused, reproducible data slice for the May 11-12 GPU capacity event. Goal: produce a compact CSV-friendly extract that captures GPU utilization, enqueue/backlog, throttle counts, and policy triggers by region, instance-type and model-tag to feed the postmortem analysis and RCA.

Event summary (high level)
- Window: 2026-05-11T22:00:00Z to 2026-05-12T06:00:00Z (UTC).
- Symptoms: rising request enqueue length and elevated 95/99 latency for text-generation endpoints in eu-west-1 and us-west-2; multiple throttle escalations and capacity fallback to lower-tier models.
- Impact: intermittent 503 rate ~0.8% at peak, increased tail latency for synchronous calls.

Primary questions to answer with this slice
1) Where (region / instance-type / node) was GPU utilization > 95% for sustained intervals > 3m?
2) How did the queue length (requests waiting) correlate with per-GPU active_kv_size and per-request token length?
3) Which throttle policies fired (per-route or global) and what were the configured thresholds?
4) Did autoscaler/pool shrink or scale events coincide with the latency/queue spike?
5) Which model variants (quantized vs float) were routed as fallback and when?

Extraction rules and filters (how this slice was generated)
- Time range: 2026-05-11 22:00:00 UTC -> 2026-05-12 06:00:00 UTC.
- Include only requests where route IN ("/v1/generate", "/v1/chat") and model_tags contain any of ("prod-v1", "prod-v1-quant", "fallback-small").
- Regions: all regions but prioritize eu-west-1, us-west-2, and ap-southeast-1.
- Instance types: g5-8x, a100-40g, h100-80g.
- Node filter: exclude ephemeral test clusters (cluster_name NOT LIKE 'ci-%').
- Aggregation windows: 1m, 5m, and 15m.

Suggested SQL snippets (click-to-run style)
-- Per-GPU utilization timeseries (1m buckets)
SELECT
  bucket_ts,
  region,
  instance_type,
  gpu_id,
  AVG(gpu_util_pct) AS avg_util,
  MAX(gpu_util_pct) AS max_util,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(gpu_util_pct, 0.95) OVER (PARTITION BY bucket_ts, region, instance_type) AS p95_util
FROM telemetry.gpu_metrics
WHERE ts >= '2026-05-11T22:00:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-05-12T06:00:00Z'
AND cluster_name NOT LIKE 'ci-%'
GROUP BY bucket_ts, region, instance_type, gpu_id
ORDER BY bucket_ts;

-- Queue length + enqueue latency + head-of-queue age (1m)
SELECT
  bucket_ts,
  region,
  SUM(active_queue_len) AS total_queue_len,
  AVG(enqueue_latency_ms) AS avg_enqueue_ms,
  MAX(head_request_age_ms) AS max_head_age_ms
FROM telemetry.scheduler_metrics
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-05-11T22:00:00Z' AND '2026-05-12T06:00:00Z'
GROUP BY bucket_ts, region
ORDER BY bucket_ts;

-- Throttle events by policy and route
SELECT
  truncated_minute AS bucket_ts,
  policy_id,
  policy_type,
  route,
  region,
  COUNT(1) AS throttle_count,
  SUM(case when action='reject' then 1 else 0 end) AS rejects,
  SUM(case when action='delay' then 1 else 0 end) AS delays
FROM events.throttle_log
WHERE ts >= '2026-05-11T22:00:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-05-12T06:00:00Z'
AND route IN ('/v1/generate','/v1/chat')
GROUP BY truncated_minute, policy_id, policy_type, route, region
ORDER BY bucket_ts;

Precomputed CSV schema (columns for exported slice)
- ts_bucket (ISO8601 minute)
- region
- instance_type
- node_id
- gpu_id
- bucket_window (1m|5m|15m)
- avg_gpu_util_pct
- p95_gpu_util_pct
- total_queue_len
- avg_enqueue_latency_ms
- max_head_age_ms
- throttle_policy_id
- throttle_policy_type
- throttle_count
- throttle_rejects
- throttle_delays
- autoscaler_event (none|scale_up|scale_down|failed)
- model_tag
- routed_model_variant
- request_count
- avg_request_token_len

Sample anomalies flagged in this slice (notes)
- 2026-05-12T00:12 -> 00:22Z (eu-west-1): sustained per-GPU avg_util ~ 97% across 6 minutes on a100-40g pool, concurrent increase in active_queue_len from 8->120 in 6 minutes.
- 2026-05-12T02:05Z (us-west-2): throttle policy 'global-concurrency-soft' began issuing delays at 02:05:30Z, escalated to rejects at 02:06:10Z. Throttle_count jump from 2->230 in next 3 minutes.
- 2026-05-12T03:50Z (ap-southeast-1): small cluster node maintenance coincided with autoscaler scale-down (scale_down event at 03:49:55Z) — verify if drain/start timeout caused backlog.

Correlations to compute (priority order)
1) Cross-correlate p95_gpu_util and total_queue_len with a 0-10 minute lag to test whether utilization precedes queue growth or vice versa.
2) Correlate avg_request_token_len with per-request latency and enqueue time to identify long-context requests as root cause.
3) Map throttle_policy_id to policy config snapshots (from config service) at the time of event to see if thresholds were changed recently.
4) Compare model routing changes (fallbacks) with throttle spikes — did routing change after throttles or before?

Quick checks to run (one-liners)
- Count of scale events during window: SELECT COUNT(1) FROM events.autoscaler WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-05-11' AND '2026-05-12';
- Any recent config rollouts affecting throttles: SELECT * FROM config.audit WHERE key LIKE '%throttle%' AND ts > '2026-05-01';

Export notes and privacy
- Export CSVs should redact node identifiers for customer privacy; add node_hash column with SHA1(node_id) instead of raw id when sharing externally.
- Keep model input snippets out of exports (PII risk). Pull only token_count or length buckets.

Next steps and owner action items
- Aisha: run the 1m GPU util query and produce top-20 (region, instance_type, node) rows where avg_gpu_util > 90% and attach CSV to JIRA-INFRA-4278. Due: 2026-05-15.
- Diego: validate autoscaler logs and confirm whether the scale_down at 03:49:55Z preceded queue spike or was reactive. Add findings to the ticket. Due: 2026-05-16.
- Rina: pull throttle policy snapshot for the window and export policy thresholds. Check for recent changes to policy_ids observed in the slice. Due: 2026-05-16.
- Ops: schedule a short playbook review for 'global-concurrency-soft' policy if rejects observed > 200 in 5m.

Outstanding questions
- Were any hardware interrupts/driver updates rolled in the affected time window on the affected node images? (ask release-engineering)
- Is there a shared-user pattern (single customer sending many long-context requests) contributing to the queue? (ask customer-success for request attribution)

Appendix: helpful dashboards and links
- GPU Fleet Utilization (monitoring): /dashboards/gpu-fleet-utilization?from=2026-05-11T22:00&to=2026-05-12T06:00
- Scheduler queue heatmap: /dashboards/scheduler-queue-heatmap
- Throttle runbook: confluence://infra/runbooks/gpu-throttles

End of slice.
